column8: Thu 19 Nov: 3a pedigree, one clause at most: FAS 76 para 3(c) read at source today, the closest any rulebook came to calling her ten paid years early; supersedes H8-020's unchecked wording; never defeased or escrowed for her holdings (Q152-036, Q31-001).
Thu 19 Nov: store; the 4-3 vote and the dissent are history, not evidence about Treasuries; half a clause at most, and only beside row 1.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.0, ink's second half from a 1983 rule (risk free as to amount, timing and collection, in the debt's own currency), which fills the half Q157-042 left open and shows why VT is owned but pencil; fix: use the rule's reason, never its asset list, which the five fund payments and the late-2032 fund fail by letter, so never imply the funds are pencil (Q54-045); FAS 76's monetary-asset footnote is unread, so VT failing it is inference; Q20-023 holds the same quotes bar the currency clause.

Thu 19 Nov: 3b or 3e: the stated figure is matched in its own currency, and the building's cost in Taiwan dollars is why IPS l.15 keeps half for a stronger Taiwan dollar; a clean reason from a verified rule (Keel synthesis); never VT as a Taiwan-dollar hedge.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c store: the 1983 board tied its certainty word to what is held because a near-absolute probability test was unworkable, as Laura's certain after the move rests on holdings, not a model (NUMBERS 4); never remote in her words (Q120-036).

Thu 19 Nov: 3a pedigree beside aha 5: FAS 76 asked only to minimize reliance on reinvestment, and the extra Treasuries remove it (NUMBERS 2); fix: never as IPS l.11 promises, since the zero-interest standard is the report's answer, not l.11's words (CANON A4).
Thu 19 Nov: store; no, yes, no in fourteen years shows the question is hard, not a slogan; the SEC's independent-trustee point is one more part of the legal shell Laura lacks (Q54-042).
Thu 19 Nov: store; the opposite motive (a gain shown against a dependence removed) is true, but the card itself bars setting the two ratios side by side; a known textbook case.
Thu 19 Nov: store; Exxon's own 10-K shows the removed debt and the trust both stayed Exxon's, proof of the reason FASB later gave; no report job beyond row 11.
Thu 19 Nov: store, colour; only the first paragraph read; no report job.

Thu 19 Nov: 3a pedigree: FAS 125's if and only if, read at source, fills H3-011's unverified rule and is why the report's verbs are set aside and does not depend, never paid before each January; one clause with row 1 at most.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e store: the Codification's reasons, read as quoted by Deloitte and PwC; reason 1 (the debtor makes up any shortfall) is the one case both of IPS l.17's reasons describe, reason 4 is what comes back from the extra Treasuries; reasons 2-3 need a lender Laura does not have.

Thu 19 Nov: 3a or 3e, one clause: the relation is already Q111-019's (the two reasons are money from outside failing to arrive), this adds accounting pedigree; fix: both of l.17's reasons are the one case FASB names (the set-aside proving short), never the cases accounting names; add if cash waiting earns nothing to the $39,162 (NUMBERS 8u c); never only two things can break the plan (Q109-033).
Thu 19 Nov: store; the rule was withdrawn partly because it flattered the books, and Laura books no gain; no report job.

Thu 19 Nov: 3d: FASB's reason for disclosing set-aside money (what is unavailable for anything else) maps to telling co-sponsors what is spoken for, her figure already in Treasuries; fix: never size or state her flexibility to them, since it is the pencil co-sponsors never see (CONCEIT 3b) and 3d says one figure; co-sponsors are not creditors.

Thu 19 Nov: store only; abstract read, and the evidence is mixed (Li 1998); the second lesson overreads it, so never use it as evidence that co-sponsors will discount her figure; the first lesson (safety costs the one who sets money aside) is already IPS l.11's trade.
Thu 19 Nov: 3a store, the plainest line on the card (a trust ensures timely servicing, it does not extinguish the liability); a critic's summary and a wording point for the verbs, so fit 2.
Thu 19 Nov: store, background only; whether IFRS 9 carries AG59 unchanged is unread.

Thu 19 Nov: 3a: the public-sector standard says a government that sets its own money aside in matched Treasuries has sufficiently met its obligations (GASB 86, read at source), the nearest named verdict on IPS l.11's structure, and its break (trust and escrow agent) is Q54-042's same arithmetic, not the same legal standing; fix: fits the T-bond payments, while whether fund shares qualify is unread (the card's Gaps), so never Laura's case exactly; never defeased or escrowed for her holdings (Q152-036).
Thu 19 Nov: store; SLGS are for refundings, so open-market Treasuries are what a body paying debt from its own money buys; trivia for the report.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q3b-033 (the wall is a policy, not a law): GASB 86's duty to disclose an unforbidden swap is outside pedigree for 3e saying so once; a caveat, so fit 2.

Thu 19 Nov: 3a or 3f: GASB saw the cost of setting its own money aside and declined to measure it, and the report measures it; say which cost is meant, forgone money (NUMBERS 8s, never the 27 Sep model's $19,000 alone) or the chance of a miss (about 1 in 31 against none).

Thu 19 Nov: 3c pedigree for the conceit's rule: a defeasance dated 6 Oct 2026 runs money, then proof, then the word, as Laura states a figure only once it is owned (IPS l.15); bond readers know the sequence (aha test 8: pedigree), so one clause; never escrowed or defeased for her holdings.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q173-023: the standard deemed-paid clause; Laura is no issuer.
Thu 19 Nov: 3a store, Taiwan's own answer: a payment counts as made early only when it is due and the creditor will not take it; comparison only, since Taiwan law is outside the case.
Thu 19 Nov: store; precedent summaries behind row 25: settled means the creditor's to take, and Laura's Treasuries are hers to take.

Thu 19 Nov: store only; the case calls the ten commitments others will rely on and leaves Taiwan's legal structure out of scope, so never say the ten are a debt she owes herself or that nothing is owed.

Thu 19 Nov: 3a framing candidate, one clause: across three systems settled means the risk has moved off the payer, and Laura keeps hers on purpose; fix: not the one risk she keeps, since fund costs past the margin and broker delay are hers too (Q109-033); GASB treats risk as moved once remote, so say three systems read.

Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q3b-033: in law her ten are at her free disposal and only IPS l.17 limits them, so the law's two states map to the plan's two kinds of money only through her rule; a Quistclose trust needs a lender, and the IPS is not a trust.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q106-009 (Pacioli: get written evidence from the other party's book); its practical point stays findable: in 2031 co-sponsors see the broker's statement, not her own sheet.
Thu 19 Nov: store only until Pacioli's chapter 36 is read in his own words; a paraphrase seen in an excerpt, and CONCEIT already warns against lines wrongly given to Pacioli.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c store: the range read by the money tests (bottom set aside from January 2028, top only after the move, the half kept never), an accounting reason for IPS l.15's order; restates the conceit's dates, so pedigree; the floor's payout is not fixed, never a fixed $150,000.
Thu 19 Nov: 2.0 and 3a date guard: most of each payment owned from January 2027 and all ten from January 2028 (NUMBERS 8u, CONCEIT), never defeased; a correction, so fit 2.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.3 (or 3c's deletion-test clause), the card's strongest and the round's best kind of find: the Supreme Court's words on the pencil with an eraser (each part performs its own duty, and nothing else) state the deletion test (NUMBERS 4: VT at zero, all ten paid, one figure, $95,000) and put the plan on the other side of the line from 1987's tied rule; cold-test it as an aha; not in 3e beside rub out every pencil line; never CPPI or portfolio insurance said of the plan.

Thu 19 Nov: the break that teaches, only with row 1 and in the same passage: the court says changing the order of use is no invention, yet the plan's merit is its order (promised money bought first, IPS l.11, l.13, l.15; the order-of-purchase reserve); the one interaction, the 2031 move, is dated, not priced.

Thu 19 Nov: merged into H2-071 (portfolio insurance rejected, the minimum bought, not insured); its new frame is row 1's; one clause at most and never CPPI or portfolio insurance said of the plan, even to deny it at length.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.2, a fact behind the working word, one clause: hand lettering went in after pencils and before inks, so the words had their room before anything permanent, as the 2028 deposit's fixed order gives the promises their room before VT gets what is left (IPS l.13, l.15); from Laura's own trade; its break (comics reserve room in pencil, Laura buys hers) travels with it.

Thu 19 Nov: 3f, a fact behind the turn the first plan's payments were in pencil, never its reason (IPS l.9's, CANON A3) and no outside name in 3f (panel 4): art first, words fitted last, all ten bought on 1 Jan 2033 and short in about 1 in 31 (NUMBERS 8s, checked); witty but tightly constrained.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q174-004 as its break: a reservation that must be remembered can fail, and Laura's is bought, so the ten are owned before anything else.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q44-020: light-blue placement pencil is non-photo blue's job (the models), which Q114-021 now carries with no trade word; one of them at most.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.0, the one fact that explains the conceit's hardest case without law: pencil and India ink are the same carbon held differently, so ink is the same dollars bound to a Treasury and a date, and VT is owned but pencil (Q157-042); its break stays: her binding is a rule kept (IPS l.17), so never cannot move; behind the definition, never staged.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q174-008: the mechanism quotes (graphite sits on the paper, ink goes into the fibres) behind same carbon, different binding; never cannot move.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c, a plain gloss for inked before the 2031 meetings: the move changes what half of VT's value is bound to, not how much there is (IPS l.15); never that the move adds safety to the amount (it buys less than a top stated a year early in about 11 of 100 futures, NUMBERS 4: 10.6%).

Thu 19 Nov: store; the Electoral Commission's line (the process, not the medium) cuts against the conceit if staged, since it treats pen and pencil as equal; at most behind 3e's custody clause; the FOI wording read only via Full Fact.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.0 or 3d store; true and from her genre, but naming a signature beside the definition brought the signed reading in (voice round 7), and Table 1 is the WInS portfolio scaled, not her record, so never co-sponsors check Table 1's CUSIPs (they would see her broker's holdings); row 13 carries the Lejeune relation better.

Thu 19 Nov: 3d, one clause behind her side of the sum is exact: Lejeune, theorist of the genre she writes in, calls limiting the oath to what one can know a supplementary proof of honesty, as Laura states only what she owns; fix: never narrow on purpose, start low or under-promise (Q154), say she states only what she owns and keeps the rest promised to no one; one Lejeune row at most, never pact in her words.
Thu 19 Nov: 3d store, the break of row 13 (a memoir can be badly kept, a journalist's text cannot), so a stated figure meets the journalist's standard; one Lejeune row at most in the report.

Thu 19 Nov: Client Knowledge, checked in the case file, but the card cuts the quote short: the case says a response to misinformation and anti-Asian racism, so quote it whole or not at all; it ties row 13 to her record.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c or 3d reserve, the same relation as 3b's ink only goes one way, so never in the same part as that turn; fix: a stated figure is booked committed by the campaign's or residency's gift office, never a co-sponsor's (Q147-001's rater); never map a fund to iron gall.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q174-016: dates only, colour on their own.
Thu 19 Nov: refuse for the report: colour, a writers' note only; the forgers' icons map to nothing in Laura's plan.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q174-020: the same pentimento fact; 3f already tells the change plainly.

Thu 19 Nov: 3f store: a visible change of mind marks an original (pentimenti help attribution), which 3f shows by telling the first plan plainly under its own cause; no outside name in 3f (panel 4), so a fact behind the telling at most.
Thu 19 Nov: refuse: a writers' process note only, read in an unchecked web transcription; no mapping onto the plan.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e, one clause at most: tattoo ink outlasts every cell that holds it, as Treasuries held for her outlast a failed broker (Lehman, 110,000 accounts in ten days, Q2a-022; MF Global, 39 days, Q72-017), so the risk above SIPC is delay; a mouse study; never identified or in her name; 3e has its turn, so a fact behind a word only.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q174-022: the graft study is the same relay; UCC 8-503 comment 2 already sits behind owned.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.0, a fact behind owned: hired orchestral parts take erasable pencil only, and only a bought score keeps markings, so ink is for owners; its break (VT owned yet pencil) shows owned is needed but not enough; competes with Q114-021 and Q133-028, one at most.
Thu 19 Nov: refuse: colour, the card's own verdict; no mapping onto the plan.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.3, the fact behind the working word in one eraser, three lines: the eraser was made for pencil marks (Priestley 1770, as quoted by Britannica), so promised money sits where it cannot reach; Priestley's own text read only in quotation; never rub out in 2.3.
Thu 19 Nov: store; a clever inversion (England guarded the pencil's source, the plan guards only the ink and leaves VT to the market, IPS l.17), but it maps loosely and needs explaining.

Thu 19 Nov: unverified (a secondary quotation of a book not read), and the fact runs against the conceit: drawings went out in pencil because inking took too long, so at most a disanalogy; read Petroski before any use.
Thu 19 Nov: refuse: colour only, the card's own verdict; Petroski unread.
